text:
sam.kim: :rotating_light: Pager alert - dedicated-pool 'orion-dedicated-a' showing sustained GPU saturation for tenant OrionLabs. GPU util 99%, queue ~1400. This looks tenant-localized.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT OPEN 3 Sev 2  dedicated pool saturation (tenant=OrionLabs)  runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-gpu-exhaustion  incident=INC-20260315-1130  paging oncall@sre

leo_sre: I'm taking lead. pulling traces and per-tenant metrics. Confirmed: traffic spike from OrionLabs started 2026-03-15T11:25Z, sustained high RPS and many 64k token eval batches. Other tenants on same pool show normal latency.

ops-bot: POOL CHECK  orion-dedicated-a  reserved_for=OrionLabs isolation_mode=tenant_isolation autoscale=false burst_allowed=false spare_capacity=0

infra-zoe: infra view: no node OOMs or hardware errors. Scheduler backlog growing. We have 4 shards pinned to OrionLabs across 10 GPUs. Eden (shared-pool) has 2 spare nodes in us-west but routing/orchestration needs manual permission to rebalance.

cs_maya: I informed OrionLabs contacts. They say they kicked off a big internal eval and are willing to pause but only if we coordinate; they do not want failovers that cause auth or IP changes.

leo_sre: options: A) request exec approval to allow a one-time burst into shared pool B) throttle OrionLabs traffic (client-side cooperation needed) C) migrate other non-enterprise tenants off the physical nodes to free GPUs (transient tenant-shed) D) route heavy batch evals to a quantized micro-model.

pm-oliver: Contractually, OrionLabs reserved 12 GPUs. Bursting into shared capacity requires legal/exec signoff. We should avoid that if we can do a surgical mitigation. Product note: tenant-shed is supported but will cause momentary increases for moved tenants.

leo_sre: propose sequence: 1) enable quantized eval routing for OrionLabs for batch workloads 2) perform targeted eviction of low-priority pods (non-enterprise) on the 4 GPUs hosting Orion shards to free 3 GPUs 3) set temporary tenant-level RPS cap for Orion to protect control plane. If queue doesn't come down in 8m, escalate to exec for burst.

sam.kim: sounds good. Execute step 3 then 2 then 1? We should reach out to the tenants we're evicting first.

ops-bot: ACTION - apply_tenant_rps  tenant=OrionLabs  rps=40  applied_by=leo_sre  ts=2026-03-15T11:34:12Z

ops-bot: ACTION DONE  tenant_rps_limit set.

infra-zoe: preparing eviction list: tenants on nodes gpu-3,gpu-4: beta-startup, demo-team, internal-loadtest. I'll message owners. Evicting non-critical pods now. Commands:```kubectl cordon node/gpu-3 && kubectl drain node/gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

ops-bot: NOTIFICATION  tenant_eviction_start  nodes=[gpu-3,gpu-4]  initiated_by=infra-zoe

beta-owner: @infra-zoe saw your note, pausing our load. thanks.

infra-zoe: eviction completed on gpu-3 and gpu-4. Freed 3 GPUs from lower-priority tenants. Kubernetes rescheduled their pods onto shared-pool nodes.

ops-bot: RESOURCE UPDATE  freed_gpus=3  pool=orion-dedicated-a  ts=2026-03-15T11:39:51Z

leo_sre: immediate effect: queue dropped 1400 -> 420 in 3 minutes. p95 latency down from 2.1s -> 340ms for small requests. Large batch evals still queueing.

pm-oliver: product request: create clearer UI and policy for emergency tenant-shed so customers know which tenants we can migrate and what the UX will be. Logged.

leo_sre: step 1 next: deploy quantized eval routing for OrionLabs (prefer micro-quant 4-bit) for batch models only. infra-zoe you can flip routing flag?

infra-zoe: deploying quant-canary for OrionLabs... ```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/orion-serve QUANT_FALLBACK=true
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/orion-serve -w
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY  orion-quant-canary  initiated_by=infra-zoe  image=models/orion-q4:rev17  ts=2026-03-15T11:44:03Z

infra-zoe: canary looks healthy, routing 20% batch traffic. Batch latency for quant requests ~180ms, queue reduced to 120.

cs_maya: OrionLabs replied: "Slowed our job by 30% internally. Thanks for the quick action. We'll coordinate a controlled ramp-down in 45m."

leo_sre: good. keep alert rule active: if queue > 800 for 10m -> page SRE lead + PM + CS. I've added a tag to incident: mitigation=tenant-shed+quant-fallback.

ops-bot: ALERT RULE CREATED  name=Orion_HighQueue  expr=tenant_queue_orionlabs > 800  for=10m  created_by=leo_sre

pm-oliver: also note: runbook update needed: clarify tenant-isolation flags and recommended emergency steps (tenant-shed pattern).

leo_sre: handoff: I'll be on until 11:50Z then handing to night oncall @sre_night. Please watch for regression. I'll draft preliminary timeline and RCA items.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE  status=mitigated  severity=P3  incident=INC-20260315-1130  ts=2026-03-15T11:50:00Z

cs_maya: scheduled post-incident call with OrionLabs for 2026-03-16T15:00Z. Will include PM and SRE.

leo_sre: owners: leo_sre (primary RCA), infra-zoe (infra follow-up), pm-oliver (product backlog), cs_maya (customer comms). Action items: 1) update runbook 2) evaluate emergency-burst product add-on 3) add telemetry to flag large token-count batches per-tenant 4) document tenant-shed UX and consent model.

sam.kim: thanks team. Closing active mitigation thread; leave monitoring on. :white_check_mark: 

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (active mitigations paused)  incident=INC-20260315-1130  ts=2026-03-15T12:03:20Z

leo_sre: will post a short summary and timeline in #incidents and link to the RCA doc once ready. If queue climbs again, escalate immediately.

cs_maya: sending customer update email now.

sam.kim: nice work.
